terra.problem: “I know angels” suggests personal familiarity with more angels than the one in Papa Dorin’s backstory.
The explanation is generic and repeats that the towns are in the text without adding much personality or insight.
There is no clear reason Papa would love to say the crowd called Barnabas Baal. The joke does not make sense.
“Wrong crowd, wrong god” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
Calling Paul a man who started churches adds a Bible fact not stated in this passage and gives no reference for it.
The text does not establish that Paul and Barnabas had not heard about the plan by the time the priest brought the bulls and wreaths.
“Nobody walked slowly or whispered” asserts details the text does not give.
Papa guesses what the individual baker was picturing.
The passage does not say the crowd saw these things all year.
The text says Paul left the next day; it does not give an elapsed time of one day.
“Other towns went that way” implies other cities drove Paul and Barnabas out. That is not stated in this passage, and no outside reference is given.
The text says they returned, but does not say they walked back.
“The ones who stayed” adds that these disciples had remained there, which the passage does not state.
The passage does not say the disciples being encouraged had themselves experienced trouble.
The explanation identifies the people entrusted to the Lord as the new elders, while the text leaves “them” open.
The statement that Caesarea appears in Acts is a Bible fact outside the passage and needs a reference.
The explanation is generic and largely restates the answer without Papa’s personality.
Saying the whole trip was about Gentiles narrows the journey beyond what the text says; it also describes Jews believing.
The statement that Samaritans appear elsewhere in Acts needs a reference.
The statement that Levites are a group in the Bible needs a reference outside this passage.
